title: The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds
source: Musée du Louvre, Paris (public domain). Wikimedia Commons: Le Tricheur à l'as de carreau - Georges de La Tour - Musée du Louvre Peintures RF 1972 8.jpg
caption: Three people are robbing him at the card table. Can you spot how? #arthistory #history #painting #art #museum
_verify: Louvre RF 1972-8, about 1635 (Wikipedia EN, The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds); a second version is in the Kimbell Art Museum.
'Three temptations' (gambling, wine, lust) is the usual reading, not La Tour's own words.
That the woman's eyes signal to the cheat is an interpretation.

slides.headline: Three people are robbing him. Can you see how?
slides.sub: Georges de La Tour, The Cheat with the Ace of Diamonds, about 1635

slides.headline: The game
slides.text: A rich young man in fine silks sits down to play cards. He thinks he is winning. He is about to lose everything.

slides.headline: The cheat
slides.text: But look at the man on the left. Behind his back, tucked into his belt, he is pulling out an ace of diamonds.

slides.headline: The look
slides.text: The woman in the middle doesn't turn her head. Only her eyes slide sideways, giving the signal to her partner.

slides.headline: The servant
slides.text: Meanwhile the servant pours more wine to keep him distracted. Cards, wine and a woman: three classic temptations.

slides.headline: The victim
slides.text: He stares at his cards, calm and sure of himself. He has no idea that everyone at this table is against him.

slides.headline: The coins
slides.text: In front of him, his gold coins wait on the table. In a few seconds they will slide to the other side.

slides.headline: The hands
slides.text: Now look at all the hands: pointing, pouring, hiding a card. In this silent painting, the hands tell the whole story.

slides.headline: Would you notice?
slides.text: La Tour painted it as a warning to rich young men. Would you have spotted the trick in time, or lost everything?
